text:
Alex C.: Heads up — on new model bring-up (hf/model-x-2.1-quant) I'm seeing streaming responses get truncated early when the chat template includes multiple stop markers (e.g. '<|end|>' and '==').
Maria G.: Oof, saw something similar with the quantized q4f8 build. Is this the HF->Redwood conversion step or the runtime streaming matcher?
Alex C.: Repro steps: converted with our hf-convert script, default special tokens: 
```json
{"eos_token": "</s>", "additional_special_tokens": ["<|end|>", "=="]}
```
Then chat template: stop = ["<|end|>", "=="]. Streaming returns tokens in chunks; on chunk boundary we got a single '=' at end of chunk A and another '=' at beginning of chunk B — runtime detected '==' in the decoded stream and closed early, even though token boundaries split it.
Joel R.: So matcher is string-based on the decoded bytes, not token-id aligned? That would explain boundary hits.
Sophia L.: Yep. We currently do pattern search on the incremental decoded text buffer to avoid waiting for full tokens. That was to keep latency low, but it's fragile with multi-char markers.
Maria G.: Also noticed tokenization weirdness: when quantized model uses byte-pair, '==' sometimes tokenizes to two separate subtokens or to a single special token depending on vocabulary. HF's tokenizer sometimes treats '==' as an 'additional_special_token' and maps to a single id, but our conversion leaves duplicates.
Alex C.: Example log: 
```
STREAM CHUNK 1: "Hello, here's the result ="
STREAM CHUNK 2: "= and then more text"
RUNTIME: detected stop marker '==' -> closing stream
```
Alex C.: The '==' was a visual match but belonged to two separate tokens crossing chunks; closing there removes trailing real text. Bad.
Joel R.: Two immediate fixes: 1) Make streaming matcher token-aware (preferable) — only stop if the marker aligns to token boundaries, or if the token-id sequence matches. 2) Update convert script to canonicalize special tokens so markers map consistently (avoid duplicate textual markers).
Sophia L.: Token-id matching is safer. Downside: if clients provide stop sequences as text, we'd need to convert those to token id sequences per model/tokenizer at request time — small overhead but acceptable.
Maria G.: For a quick mitigation we could implement a config flag like `stream.deferred_stop = true` that waits until the last token from a chunk is complete before scanning for textual markers. That reduces false positives without the full id-path.
Alex C.: Also, there are edge cases with multiple EOS tokens in config.json. Some HF models set both `eos_token_id` and include the same symbol in `additional_special_tokens`, which confuses our converter. We should normalize by: if additional_special_tokens contains the same text as eos_token, remove duplicates and ensure eos_token_id is set on output config.
Joel R.: I'll open a PR to change the streaming matcher to token-id sequence matching and add a fast path fallback: if client passed textual stops and tokenizer mapping fails, fallback to deferred textual matching.
Sophia L.: I'll update hf-convert to dedupe special tokens and emit a `streaming_safe_stop_texts` array that maps to canonical token-id sequences in the model metadata. That way runtime can look up token sequences quickly.
Maria G.: Can we also add a quick test in our eval harness? A short harness that forces chunk boundaries on the '=' split and asserts the stream continues until an explicit EOS token id is seen. eval-bot: scheduled regression test "streaming-stop-boundary" added to nightly, runs on q4f8 and fp16.
Alex C.: Work items: Joel - token-id matcher + fallback (priority P1). Sophia - hf-convert dedupe + metadata (P1). Maria - add harness (P2). I'll patch the hosted runtime flag for deferred_stop as emergency mitigation (P0) so we can flip it for effected customers.
Joel R.: One more note: quantization can change tokenization alignment slightly if we swap vocab files inadvertently during packaging. Double-check that the vocab.json and merges/tokenizer files are the ones shipped in the HF repo, not the trimmed ones from earlier conversion steps.
Maria G.: Agreed. I'm going to re-run conversion with a strict checksum check and attach diffs.
Alex C.: Thanks. If anyone hits a production case, flip `stream.deferred_stop=true` in customer runtime and we should avoid truncation while we roll out the token-id matcher. :thumbsup:
Sophia L.: I'll leave a TODO to document best practices for model authors: avoid ambiguous short stop markers like '==' when using streaming unless you guarantee tokenization as a single token.
deploy-bot: deploy queued for runtime flag patch (deploy/stream-deferred-stop) by Alex C..
Alex C.: Cool, I'll follow up with PR links in this thread when they're up.
